Off that rig there is no window, every Paint returns a typed refusal and every proof string is empty - so a comparison keyed to the machine property would be two empty strings agreeing with each other about a surface that was never created, which is precisely the vacuity this list exists to prevent. skipSemantics: May-skip, not must-skip: a listed test that runs and passes on a machine where its precondition holds is green. Matching is exact on the pre-'(' portion of the TRX result testName (xunit theory rows serialize with arguments, e.g. Class.Method(x: 1)); a name with no parens matches whole. Anchor is the TRX result list, never Counters arithmetic.
admissionRule: allowedSkips is not a quarantine list. A test may be listed only when its precondition is a property of the machine or OS that cannot be satisfied by configuration during a contract run, and its change names the machine class where it executes. Two named PERMANENT BANS apply: (1) CcpClient.Tests.DataRootOverrideTests.DefaultSettingsPath_EnvUnset_IsThePlatformDefault must never be allowed to skip because a process-wide CCP_DATA_ROOT override makes the floor vacuous; (2) CcpClient.Tests.ChaosTunnelLoopbackTests.Logging_RouteClassesOnly_NeverFilenameOrQuery must be fixed at the source, never quarantined.
bumpRule: Bump total only in the same commit as the test change that moves the count, with the reason recorded here. Never widen, disable, or special-case a check to make a step pass. Adding a name to allowedSkips requires the admission rule above and the machine class where it executes.
lastMovedBy: +4 unit, headless unchanged at 289: THE DEFAULTS SWEEP, and the general lesson turned out broader than the finding that prompted it. All 37 Default* constants in Effects/ and Session/ were compared against upstream, and THE CLEAN ROWS ARE REPORTED TOO so nobody repeats the sweep. ONLY ONE CONSTANT IN THE TREE HAD XAML AS ITS SOLE PROVENANCE AND IT WAS THE DEFECT: MandatoryVideoSchedule.DefaultPerHour, taken from a slider Value of 2 that is overwritten on load, against the settings model's 6. Fixed. Its sibling constant already named the identical trap and resolved it correctly, and five more rows are the INVERSE error the packet warned about - constants that legitimately come from markup or a codec fallback because upstream has no settings equivalent, correct rather than defects. A COMMENT THAT LIED ABOUT UPSTREAM WAS CORRECTED WITHOUT CHANGING ITS VALUE: MandatoryVideoPresetDocument asserted 'Ships OFF' where upstream ships it ON, and now records both upstream's value and the port's deliberate divergence, sequenced behind the open white-screen defect because enabling it puts an opaque full-monitor surface on by default. THE LANE WIDENED THE CRITERION RATHER THAN THE FILE SCOPE, and that is where the value was: it found a second mismatch of the same class in different clothes - BrainDrainSchedule.DefaultIntensity taken from a SERVICE FIELD INITIALIZER that Start() overwrites, which is a design-time placeholder for exactly the reason a XAML literal is, and sweeping only markup would have missed it. IT DID NOT FIX IT, CORRECTLY: upstream contradicts ITSELF across three sites - settings say 20, the service field says 50, and Preset.cs says 50 AND writes it back into settings on every preset apply - so my rule 'fix a plain number whose only consequence is matching upstream' has its precondition fail when upstream has two numbers. Pinned with both values. DECISION TAKEN: the port KEEPS 50, because it matches two of upstream's three sites and matches the path a real user takes, since applying any preset writes 50 into settings and 20 is only ever seen on a fresh install that never applies one. NO TAUTOLOGY: upstream's numbers are typed as literals checked against the file, then the port constant is compared to the READ value rather than to the literal. ALSO REPORTED AND DELIBERATELY NOT REPAIRED: seven port comments cite AppSettings.cs line numbers that have rotted - every VALUE right, only the lines moved - and eight cite a CCP.Core tree that does not exist in this repository.
